sources.title: ModelingAgent / ModelingBench + ModelingJudge
sources.notes: Closest public modeling benchmark and useful rubric design; public tasks cannot support a real-unseen claim.

sources.title: MM-Agent / MM-Bench
sources.notes: Useful external comparison, but public MCM/ICM cases and judge scores are not a sealed gold standard.

sources.title: Systematic Evaluation of LLMs vs. Human Experts in Mathematical Contest in Modeling
sources.notes: Useful stage-wise rubric and independent-human agreement methodology; public contest cases still cannot establish real-unseen accuracy.

sources.title: COMAP MCM/ICM official public problem pages
sources.notes: Good task-input source and execution regression; awards or public papers are not numerical correctness labels.

sources.title: International Math Modeling Contest official guide
sources.notes: Independent-professor judging process is useful for protocol design, but the public contest source is not a sealed unseen dataset.

sources.title: IMProofBench private uncontaminated mathematics benchmark
sources.notes: Strong unseen/private and expert-grading methodology, but proof generation is not mathematical modeling.

sources.title: Epoch FrontierMath
sources.notes: Useful contamination-control reference for original mathematics, not a modeling benchmark.

sources.title: OpenAI FrontierScience
sources.notes: Useful expert-rubric and held-out scientific reasoning methodology; not specific enough to establish modeling accuracy.

sources.title: Modeling the Future Challenge active-year scenario
sources.notes: Organizer-controlled scenario has real-world data and multi-level questions; must obtain a written evaluation partnership before treating it as a private holdout.

sources.title: International Mathematical Modeling Contest organizer-provided future problem
sources.notes: Candidate partnership route; organizer must provide an unreleased problem and an independent scoring package.

sources.title: DrivenData hidden-label predictive competitions
sources.notes: Useful for externally scored predictive accuracy with hidden labels; task-specific competition rules and leakage controls remain required, and this is not open-ended mathematical modeling.

sources.title: TML-Bench private-holdout tabular ML benchmark
sources.notes: Reports hidden-label holdout scores for data-science agents; can validate execution/prediction routing, but cannot establish expert-scored modeling quality.

sources.title: Kaggle hidden-ground-truth code competitions
sources.notes: Platform-level hidden solution/leaderboard mechanism; only a named competition with a frozen protocol can be used, and its score is a prediction metric rather than a modeling gold standard.
